memos.scout:
Best honest case for buying BRIDGE now:

The organic classification and absence of an airdrop dump are real positives. The curve shows broad participation: 274 buyers, with the top 3 holding only 12.9% and the top 5 post-graduation buyers only 11.4%. The coin is up 2.48x over 30 minutes and 1.73x in the last 15, with 1,118 buyers in that window and $190k volume, so demand has been active rather than a single wallet pumping. Pool depth of 162 SOL is reasonable for a $20 ticket.

The case is weak, though. Last 15 minutes show net flow of only 81 SOL on 839 SOL bought, with 869 sellers and a sell-to-buy ratio of 1.23 in the first two minutes after graduation, which means heavy early exit pressure. The coin is already 15% off its 30-minute high, and the 2.5x run means much of the easy move is likely priced in. Bundling is 33%, and the launch bot is present. Buying 30 to 60 minutes out, against a base rate of roughly 20% losses per trade, the signals support a watch, not a confident entry. If you want a case to buy, it requires evidence that buying has re-accelerated after the dip, which this brief does not show. I'd recommend skipping.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss path is distribution into strength. BRIDGE is up 2.48x over 30 minutes and 1.73x in the last 15, but the last-15 flow is 839 SOL bought against 758 SOL sold, with 869 sellers against 1,118 buyers. The net inflow of 81 SOL is thin for a coin this size, so most of the pump was churn. The curve shows a 32.8% bundle share and a 54% completer share, which suggests coordinated early buying that may now be exiting. The early tape is also sell-heavy (sell/buy ratio 1.23 post-graduation), and the 15% drawdown from the 30-minute high is already biting. With a 162 SOL pool, a $20 round trip faces 1.4-5.1% friction, so a 10% reversal wipes out most of any bounce. Skip.
